sourcedFrom: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. (2017 (copyright line, PDF p.40))
cleanIntro: SilencerCo asks for a field strip after every shooting session. The Maxim 50 is a break-open inline whose moderator sits on a permanent weld attachment at the muzzle: the barrel lifts off the receiver and the Accelerator Breech Plug comes out of the barrel, so the bore can be cleaned from the breech end.

steps.title: Nothing live on the bench
steps.action: Before any tool comes out, put the powder, primers and projectiles away from the bench and confirm none is in the rifle.
steps.quote: CONFIRM THERE ARE NO POWDER CHARGES, PRIMERS, OR PROJECTILES PRESENT OR AVAILABLE DURING ANY DISASSEMBLY, REASSEMBLY, OR FUNCTION TEST PROCEDURES.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Cleaning & Maintenance — p.53 (PDF p.30)
steps.warn: Uncharged and unprimed are two separate checks. A muzzleloader with no primer in the plug can still hold a full charge and a seated projectile.

steps.title: Engage the safety
steps.action: Press the safety button across until the red ring disappears. A red ring showing means the rifle is set to fire.
steps.quote: Press safety button to engage. Red ring is NOT visible when in safe position.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.55 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: De-cock and open the action
steps.action: Press down on the striker de-cocking button, or press the barrel catch lever, so the striker button returns to rest; then let the action pivot open to expose the breech plug.
steps.prose: Pressing the barrel catch lever does two jobs on this rifle: it releases a cocked striker and it unlocks the barrel to pivot open.
steps.quote: De-cock the Maxim 50 by pressing down on the striker de-cocking button or pressing barrel catch lever to de-cock gun. Open action and access breech plug.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.55 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Remove the breech plug and look through the bore
steps.action: Unscrew the Accelerator Breech Plug by hand or with the breech plug wrench, then look down the barrel from the breech end to confirm it is empty and clear.
steps.caution: Look down the barrel from the breech end, never from the muzzle. SilencerCo's own unloading check is done with the plug out, looking down the barrel from the breech end.
steps.quote: Remove the Accelerator Breech Plug™ and inspect the barrel to be sure your muzzleloader is unprimed, unloaded, and free of obstruction.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.55 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Take off the forend
steps.action: Back the forend stock screw out with the 4mm Allen wrench from the kit and lift the forend off the barrel assembly.
steps.quote: Remove forend stock screw and forend from barrel assembly using the 4mm Allen wrench provided (11A).
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.55 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Press the barrel catch lever and lift the barrel assembly up and out of the receiver. Barrel with its moderator, receiver with the stock, forend and breech plug are the pieces you clean.
steps.quote: Remove barrel from receiver by pressing the barrel catch lever and lifting up on the barrel assembly (11B).
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.55 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Brush and patch the barrel
steps.action: Wet the barrel brush with EZ Clean and scrub the bore and the outside of the barrel, then push cleaning patches through on the ramrod and jag, breech to muzzle.
steps.quote: Apply Traditions EZ Clean™ to barrel brush to clean the interior and exterior of the barrel. Run bore cleaning patches through the barrel from breech to muzzle using the ramrod and cleaning jag.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.56 (PDF p.31)
steps.warn: Do NOT pull patches back and forth through the barrel or moderator.

steps.title: Dry and protect the barrel
steps.action: Run several dry patches until the bore is dry, then leave a film of rust-inhibiting oil inside and out.
steps.quote: Dry the barrel interior with several dry bore patches. Lubricate with an oil inhibitor to protect interior and exterior surfaces of both barrel and receiver from rust and to ease loading.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.56 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Oil and grease the receiver
steps.action: Oil the inside of the receiver lightly, put a light coat of grease on the frame pivot pin and the barrel catch surface, and oil every other metal surface.
steps.prose: Grease on the pivot pin and catch, oil everywhere else: the pivot and catch carry the barrel's weight and lock-up, and grease stays where oil runs off.
steps.quote: Lightly oil inside of receiver. Lightly grease frame pivot pin and barrel catch surface. Lightly oil all interior and exterior metal surfaces.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Field Stripping & Cleaning — p.56 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Clean the breech plug and its fire channel
steps.action: Soak the plug in solvent or the EZ Clean bath, then stiff-brush the threads, the inside and the fire channel and dry it.
steps.prose: The fire channel is the hole the primer flame travels through to the charge. A channel packed with fouling is how a primer pops and the main charge does not.
steps.quote: Spray the breech plug inside and out with Traditions™ Blackout 209 cleaning solvent or use the EZ Clean™ bath system to loosen the fouling. Use a stiff brush to clean the outside threads and inner area of the breech plug including the fire channel. Dry thoroughly.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Breech Plugs — p.65 (PDF p.36)

steps.title: Grease the plug threads and o-ring
steps.action: Coat the threads and the o-ring with breech plug grease before the plug goes back in the barrel.
steps.quote: Lube the threads and o-ring with Traditions™ breech plug grease or an appropriate anti-seize grease. NOT USING THE RECOMMENDED LUBRICANT WILL CAUSE O-RING DAMAGE AND BREECH PLUG SEIZURE.
steps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Breech Plugs — p.65 (PDF p.36)
steps.warn: Be careful to not get any grease inside the breech plug.

deepSteps.title: Push out the safety button, left to right
deepSteps.action: With the barrel and forend off, use the 4mm Allen wrench as a punch and push the safety button slowly from the left side to the right, out of the buttstock.
deepSteps.quote: Locate safety button. Using your 4mm Allen wrench as a punch, slowly push safety button from left to right and remove it from the butt stock (12C).
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Disassembly — p.57 (PDF p.32)
deepSteps.warn: REMOVING THE SAFETY BUTTON FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION CAN DAMAGE YOUR SAFETY BUTTON, SPRING, AND / OR BUTTSTOCK.

deepSteps.title: Take the buttstock off the receiver
deepSteps.action: Press the butt pad's two buttons and lift it off, back the stock bolt and its washer out with the 6mm handle wrench, then slide the buttstock rearward off the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Remove butt pad using two fingers to depress the buttons (12D). Remove stock bolt and stock bolt washer with a 6mm handle wrench (12E). Carefully slide the buttstock from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Disassembly Continued — p.59 (PDF p.33)

deepSteps.title: Remove the striker assembly
deepSteps.action: Lift the striker retention spring off its pin, drive the striker retention pin fully out with a small punch, then hold the barrel catch lever down and draw the striker assembly out the rear of the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Remove striker retention spring from striker retention pin (12F). Completely remove striker retention pin from receiver using a small punch. Depress the barrel catch lever to remove striker assembly. Remove from rear of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Disassembly Continued — p.59 (PDF p.33)
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE RECEIVER. THIS INCLUDES ANY PINS HOLDING THE RECEIVER TOGETHER.

deepSteps.title: Degrease the striker channel, striker and trigger group
deepSteps.action: Mop out the striker channel, degrease the striker assembly, spray the trigger and sear on the bottom of the receiver, and clean inside the receiver ahead of the barrel catch lever.
deepSteps.quote: Clean inside of striker channel located in receiver with a 20ga bore mop or soft nylon brush lightly sprayed with degreaser/cleaner. Clean striker assembly with gun degreaser/cleaner. Spray degreaser/cleaner on trigger and sear components on bottom of receiver. Clean inside of receiver in front of barrel catch lever.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning — p.61 (PDF p.34)

deepSteps.title: Oil the striker and the mechanism, one drop at a time
deepSteps.action: Oil the striker assembly and the inside of the receiver lightly, then put one drop on each side of the trigger, sear, striker stop and mechanism pin pivot points.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly oil striker assembly (13A). Lightly oil inside of receiver. Lightly oil trigger, sear, striker stop, and mechanism pins. Apply one drop of quality gun oil to each side of the referenced parts pivot points. Do not overlubricate.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning — p.61 (PDF p.34)

deepSteps.title: Clean and protect the barrel
deepSteps.action: Brush and patch the barrel inside and out with EZ Clean, dry the bore, oil it, and grease the pivot and catch surface on the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: Apply Traditions EZ Clean™ to barrel brush and cleaning patches to clean both interior and exterior of barrel. Dry barrel interior with several dry bore patches. Lubricate with an oil inhibiting agent. Lightly grease frame pivot pin and barrel catch surface on barrel.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning — p.61 (PDF p.34)

deepSteps.title: Flush the moderator
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off the receiver, run warm water through it, first muzzle to breech and then breech to muzzle, and keep alternating until it runs clear; finish with a pass of very hot water each way.
deepSteps.quote: CLEANING THE MODERATOR The moderator portion of the Maxim 50 requires limited maintenance after every 50 – 60 rounds. Follow the field assembly steps to remove the barrel from the receiver. Then, run warm water through the barrel alternating from muzzle to breech (13A) and then from breech to muzzle (13B). Continue alternating directions until water runs clear. Pour extremely hot water from muzzle to breech, then breech to muzzle, as a final rinse.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning Continued — p.63 (PDF p.35)
deepSteps.warn: FAILING TO CLEAN THE MODERATOR MAY RESULT IN HANGFIRES OR INCOMPLETE POWDER BURN.

deepSteps.title: Dry the moderator muzzle-up
deepSteps.action: Patch the barrel dry, then stand it muzzle up so the water drains out of the baffles, and let the moderator air dry completely before the rifle is used.
deepSteps.quote: Dry barrel thoroughly with patches and allow moderator to air dry completely before use. Barrel should be left with the muzzle pointing up during the drying process to allow all water to run out of the baffles of the moderator.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning Continued — p.63 (PDF p.35)
deepSteps.warn: If the moderator and barrel are not fully dry, it may cause rust inside the barrel.

deepSteps.title: Store it dry, out of the case
deepSteps.action: Put the rifle away somewhere cool, dry and secure, not in a gun case, and check the surfaces and the bore for pitting or rust during long storage.
deepSteps.quote: Store your muzzleloader in a cool, dry, secured area. Do not store in a gun case to avoid condensation and corrosion. During long periods of storage, periodically check for signs of pitting or rusting on the surface and in the barrel bore.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Detailed Cleaning — p.61 (PDF p.34)

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly
deepSteps.action: The striker assembly is where SilencerCo's disassembly stops. Anything further goes to SilencerCo.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE MAXIM 50 BEYOND WHAT IS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL. Should further disassembly be required, contact SilencerCo’s Customer Service department at 801.417.5384.
deepSteps.cite: SILENCERCO MAXIM® 50 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — User Responsibilities Continued — p.16 (PDF p.11)

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: EZ Clean on the barrel brush, bore and exterior
Cleaning patches breech to muzzle on the ramrod and jag
Do not pull patches back and forth through the barrel or moderator
Several dry patches until the bore is dry

cleaning.name: Receiver
tasks: Light grease on the frame pivot pin and barrel catch surface
Light oil on all other metal surfaces

cleaning.name: Breech plug
tasks: Solvent inside and out, or the EZ Clean bath
Stiff-brush the threads, the inner area and the fire channel
Dry thoroughly and wipe until no residue transfers
Breech plug grease on the threads and the o-ring
Do not get grease inside the breech plug

reassembly: If the striker came out: slide the striker assembly back in from the rear of the receiver, refit the striker retention pin and its spring, slide the buttstock on, and run the stock bolt and washer back in with the 6mm wrench — the reverse of the order it came apart.
Refit the butt pad, then install the safety button from right to left. SilencerCo warns that installing it from the other direction can cause damage.
Set the barrel assembly back into the receiver and pivot it closed until you hear the metallic click of the action locking.
Refit the forend and run its stock screw back in with the 4mm Allen wrench.

Open the action, check the breech plug's fire channel is clear, and thread the greased plug into the barrel until it contacts the barrel and seats firmly. If it will not thread or seat fully, take it out and inspect the o-ring, the threads and inside the barrel for fouling.
fncheck: Run SilencerCo's function test, unloaded and pointed safely: the action opens on the barrel catch lever and locks with a click; the striker button locks forward showing the red line and the de-cocking button returns it; with the safety on and no red ring the trigger does not fire the striker; with the red ring showing it does, and the barrel catch lever returns the striker to rest. SilencerCo asks for this test any time the rifle has been taken apart for cleaning, and a striker button that will not return to rest means the rifle is not functioning properly and must be dealt with before going on.
breakOpen: press the barrel catch lever and let the action pivot open.
